source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-46: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 46 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Treat this as provisional RoCE GPU-cluster performance analysis guidance for variant 46. Assume a multi-node collective workload, but do not assume lossless behavior, GPU-direct transfers, symmetric routes, or absence of a fallback transport. Separate measured facts, estimates, and unknowns. Record GPU/NIC/switch topology, PCIe/NVLink affinity, firmware/driver/library versions, MTU, link speed, VLAN and priority mapping, queue-pair count, message-size and concurrency distributions, clock alignment, and actual transport selection. Trace the path from the collective call through verbs work requests/completions and registered host/GPU buffers to NIC, fabric, and peer; correlate application timestamps with NIC and switch counters rather than treating either as causal proof. Use reversible, single-variable canaries only after baseline capture; define an abort threshold and restore the last known-good configuration. Falsifiable hypothesis: unstable tail latency is caused by a path/configuration mismatch or congestion event rather than workload drift. Interleave matched baseline and treatment runs with fixed placement, software, warm-up, message mix, concurrency, and sample count. Measure per-rank p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency in microseconds, throughput, timeout/retry/error rates, ECN/PFC events, drops, NIC queue/completion errors, and CPU/GPU utilization; report distributions, confidence intervals or bootstrap uncertainty, and clock/timestamp limitations. Check MTU consistency and route symmetry, lossless-priority/PFC/ECN behavior, congestion and queue pressure, NIC counters, queue-pair behavior, and whether the library silently selected a fallback path. Attribute a change only when the predicted counters and latency distributions move together and correctness is unchanged. Rollback if correctness fails, timeouts/drops/retries increase, or the tail exceeds the predeclared threshold (for example 10% relative degradation); preserve artifacts and state that platform-specific counter meanings require vendor documentation. Do not claim improvement without topology, workload, baseline, synchronized telemetry, and matched-run evidence.

Trace the path from the collective call through verbs work requests/completions and registered host/GPU buffers to NIC, fabric, and peer; correlate application timestamps with NIC and switch counters rather than treating either as causal proof. Use read-only, vendor-appropriate inventory and counter collection first; redact hostnames, tokens, and credentials, and require change approval before any configuration mutation. Falsifiable hypothesis: unstable tail latency is caused by a path/configuration mismatch or congestion event rather than workload drift. Interleave matched baseline and treatment runs with fixed placement, software, warm-up, message mix, concurrency, and sample count. Measure per-rank p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency in microseconds, throughput, timeout/retry/error rates, ECN/PFC events, drops, NIC queue/completion errors, and CPU/GPU utilization; report distributions, confidence intervals or bootstrap uncertainty, and clock/timestamp limitations. Check MTU consistency and route symmetry, lossless-priority/PFC/ECN behavior, congestion and queue pressure, NIC counters, queue-pair behavior, and whether the library silently selected a fallback path. Attribute a change only when the predicted counters and latency distributions move together and correctness is unchanged. Rollback if correctness fails, timeouts/drops/retries increase, or the tail exceeds the predeclared threshold (for example 10% relative degradation); preserve artifacts and state that platform-specific counter meanings require vendor documentation. Do not claim improvement without topology, workload, baseline, synchronized telemetry, and matched-run evidence.

quality_dimensions.requirement_coverage: covers assumptions, mechanisms, boundary conditions, failure modes, measurement plan, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.technical_specificity: names RoCE, verbs/completions, topology, PFC/ECN, MTU, routing, queues, fallback, and path instrumentation
quality_dimensions.falsifiability: matched interleaved baseline, fixed confounders, explicit metrics, uncertainty, and rollback thresholds
quality_dimensions.actionability: ordered evidence collection with read-only collection or reversible canaries appropriate to the task
